Hope’s mission is to engage, encourage, and equip women and teen girlsfacing any difficult life situation.

We guide women from TRAUMA TO TRANSFORMATION!

Hope Women’s Center was founded in 1984 as a small crisis pregnancy center in Apache Junction. Today, Hope is a safe place for women and teen girls facing any difficult life situation. In addition to our original Apache Junction Center, we also have centers in the underserved communities of Phoenix, Northern Arizona, Coolidge, Maricopa, South Phoenix, and the West Valley. Our Hope on the Road partner sites allow us to serve women across Arizona.

Our programs are holistically designed to address the physical, emotional, and spiritual needs of each client. We are a faith-based nonprofit funded by partnerships with individuals, churches, civic groups, businesses, grants and foundations, and other community partners.

To learn more, visit ourVolunteerpage.

about.raw_text:
When the Anderson family became adoptive parents, they knew they wanted to help siblings in foster care stay together because of the strong relationships siblings have. They couldn’t imagine children being separated from the only people who truly understood what they were feeling.

Even after the Anderson’s adopted three siblings their commitment didn’t end. The family keeps their home ready just in case a fourth sibling is born, ensuring every sibling will have a strong relationship with each other as one family.

Brandon spent most of his life in foster care, typically moving from home to home when his behavior became too much for the family. He never felt like he had a good relationship with anyone who was a parental figure.

Then he met the Greene family who promised Brandon they were always going to be family.

Every time Brandon had a bad day or outburst his foster parents would remind him of the relationship they have. That he was still loved even if he made a mistake but they weren’t sure if he truly believed it.

That is until he was picked up from school one day. It had been a rough day and Brandon was disappointed in how he had behaved. As they drove home, his foster mom heard him whispering over and over again:

“Just because I made a mistake doesn’t mean they don’t love me.”

about.raw_text:
Read Better Be Better is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization based in Phoenix, Arizona, founded in 2014 as a response to thestate’s literacy crisis. Our mission is to equip youth with the skills to read and lead. This begins byaddressing the challenge that many 3rd graders in Arizona face, with a significant portion reading below grade level. This gap in reading proficiency often hinders their ability to transition from“learning to read” to “reading to learn” by 4th grade, impacting their academic progress and future opportunities. We believe that literacy is foundational to success in education and life, making our work vital in ensuring that every child has the opportunity to excel.

Initially starting as an afterschool reading comprehension and leadership program pairing 3rd grade readers with middle school leaders, we have expanded our reach.Today, we serve students from kindergarten through 12th gradewith our continuum of programs, called the “Changemaker Continuum.”We have added two more programs over the years to further the high school students’ leadership skills: thePathways to Education Professions Program, providing high schoolers with experience in education professions by engaging with students in a classroom setting in one of our K-8 after-school literacy programs, and thePathways to Civic Leadership Program, guiding high school students through a curriculum focused on leadership development and community engagement. Our programs not only improve reading skills but also inspire students to become leaders and changemakers in their communities, addressing broader social issues and creating a brighter future for all.

Our unique peer-led reading model not only improves reading fluency and comprehension, but also confidence and leadership skills. Readers become Leaders. Leaders become Changemakers.

At Read Better Be Better, our Changemaker Continuum inspires students at every stage of their educational journey, fostering literacy, leadership, and community engagement.
about.description: Read Better Be Better's mission is to connect young readers and youth leaders to inspire a love of literacy and learning.

The Grand Canyon State is full of natural wonder, vibrant culture, and connected communities. People are drawn to Arizona, not only for the beautiful weather, but for the state's sense of opportunity, spirit of innovation and entrepreneurship, and a willingness to embrace leaders ready to play an active role in their community.

Arizona needs these strong leaders—willing to roll up their sleeves, and work hand-in-hand with students, families, and their communities, to help raise the bar for education achievement across the state.

Arizona’s future success and economic vitality is also dependent on the rate of Latino educational attainment. Arizona is on track to be one of the first states to have a “minority” majority population, with Latinos making up the majority of the population by 2028, yet education results for Latino students remain disproportionately low.

As of the summer of 2022, there are over 2,000 teacher vacancies in the state of Arizona. We passionately believe a committed and qualified teacher can change the trajectory of a student’s achievement by investing in the talents and abilities our students possess.

Teach For America Phoenix has a proud 28 year history in Phoenix, which is represented in the strength of our community and school partnerships, and in the impact of our over 100 corps members and 1,100 alumni still living in Arizona. Informed and inspired by their students, many alumni choose to teach in high-need schools and communities beyond their two-year commitments. Others lead from many sectors that shape the context and conditions in which schools operate: they are school and district leaders; policy makers; founders of advocacy organizations; social entrepreneurs; and business, philanthropic, and civic leaders working to make change. Our corps members and alumni work relentlessly every day with our communities to ensure the students of Arizona have the opportunities they deserve.

The students of Phoenix have big plans to change the world.

Phoenix is the fifth largest city in the U.S. and the only state capital with a population of more than 1 million residents.

It's a place of rebirth, rich culture, and endless sunny days. From food trucks to hiking trails to spring training games to art exhibits, staying busy is easy. And with over 300 days of sunshine and an average winter temperature in the 0s, outdoor activities are a must!

Teach For America has had a presence in Phoenix for almost 30 years, and our alumni community is large and thriving. There are 1,100 alumni across Arizona, more than half still working in schools as teachers, school administrators, and district leaders. Alumni continue their leadership as elected officials, business leaders, health care professionals, lawyers, and other careers rooted in their experience as educators.

In the years to come, we will evolve from 1000+ big to 1000+ strong in Arizona, by strengthening the ties that bind our community, learning from many perspectives, experiences, and pathways, and empowering our network to learn, collaborate, and take action together towards excellent educational opportunities for all students n Arizona.

At TCH, our mission is to empower individuals with physical and developmental disabilities to live fulfilling lives by providing individualized programs and supports tailored to their unique needs. We strive to encourage health and wellness, promote inclusion in all aspects of community life, and increase self-esteem and confidence by ensuring each individual has the opportunity to make their own choices and direct their own paths.

Director of Human Resources

Assistant Director of Outreach and Relationships

Director of Quality Assurance and Compliance

As Chief Executive Officer, Jeff is responsible for providing long term strategic planning and day to day leadership for the organization. Jeff works with the board of directors and the executive management team to establish and achieve business objectives consistent with the core values and mission of the organization.

Jeff took his first tour of TCH’s facility in 2010 and was immediately drawn to its compelling mission. He subsequently served on the TCH board of directors for seven years, including two years as its chairman. Jeff has a B.A. from Boston University and a J.D. from the University of Arizona Rogers College of Law.

Prior to becoming TCH’s CEO, he practiced management side labor and employment law at a local and national law firm, where he held various leadership positions. In addition, Jeff was also recognized on multiple occasions as a leading lawyer in his practice area by virtually every peer and client rating service, including; Best Lawyers in America, Martindale-Hubbell, Chambers are Partners USA, and Southwest Super Lawyer.During his tenure which began in 2018, the organization has achieved substantial gains in nearly all of its programmatic and financial metrics. Additionally, during his time, TCH has self-funded and completed a significant capital improvement construction project of its entire main campus facilities; been awarded the two largest grants in its history; and, was selected by the Tempe Chamber of Commerce as its 2022 Large Business of the Year Award Winner.

Jeff is also deeply involved in the broader disability provider industry. He has been elected to and served as both Chair and Vice Chair of The Arizona Association of Providers for People with Disabilities (AAPPD). AAPPD is a state wide consortium of approximately 120 disability providers and is the leading advocacy voice for the disability community at both the Arizona Legislature and in the greater community. In 2021, Jeff received a gubernatorial appointment to the Arizona Developmental Disabilities Planning council and currently continues to serve in this role.

At Tanner Community Development Corporation (TCDC), we are dedicated to transforming communities through compassion, connection, and service. Our mission is to uplift individuals and families by offering resources, mentorship, and programs that promote growth, education, and empowerment. Guided by faith and driven by purpose, we aim to be a beacon of hope—providing help and healing to those in need

TCDC’s core initiatives are built to address the social determinants of health and uplift underserved communities through sustainable, measurable outcomes. Our Health & Wellness initiative prioritize prevention and education, empowering individuals to make informed lifestyle choices and enhance their mental well-being. Through our Youth Initiative, we help adolescents combat substance misuse by equipping them with tools to resist peer pressure and bullying. For Seniors, we offer resources that promote active aging, improve digital literacy, and provide reliable transportation—ensuring they remain engaged, connected, and supported.

Our Property Development initiative marks a bold advancement in our mission. In collaboration with Tanner Properties, TCDC is developing affordable, high-quality housing throughout the greater Phoenix area. This effort directly addresses the urgent need for stable, long-term housing—creating a foundation for healthier families, stronger neighborhoods, and more resilient communities. This strategic expansion underscores our unwavering commitment to holistic, place-based transformation.

Discover how the Tanner Community Development Corporation is making a difference—one initiative at a time. From building a village for veterans to uniting the community during tough times, these videos highlight our heart, our mission, and our impact.

about.raw_text:
Valley Leadership empowers, leverages and mobilizes leaders to meaningfully impact the most pressing issues facing Arizona.

A broad spectrum of Arizonans working together to impact the issues that matter most, setting the example on leadership.

At our core, Valley Leadership builds community. We do that by empowering a broad spectrum of Arizonans to lead through our leadership programs and activating them to make a difference on our state’s most pressing issues through Impact Maker. Our work is grounded in thePrinciples of Doing®leadership framework, which shapes how we develop leaders and engage communities across Arizona.

ThePrinciples of Doing®leadership frameworkdraws on the actions and values of the people who have made the greatest impact on our state throughout our history. With an emphasis on action, ourPrinciples of Doing®guide how Valley Leadership develops leaders through our programs and Impact Maker work, and how we engage our network to move Arizona forward.

Leadership is engaging other perspectives with respect, taking responsibility for  one's own beliefs, actions, and biases and giving others the space to do the same. Value information, facts and critical thinking. Examine your own biases when challenged (you may not always be right).

Leadership is committing to the team’s success and caring more about getting things done than who gets credit.

Leadership is taking pride in building a culture that fosters relationships, trust, and civility in order to find common ground. Be open to compromise and willing to listen to other points of view. Mutually respect one another. Have the conversation at the table.

Leadership is approaching issues from a standpoint of what is best for Arizona, not settling for a quick fix or what is best for a political party or individual ambition. Shared responsibility across many different backgrounds and interests is critical to long-term impact.

Leadership is setting the example on doing: starting with the outcome in mind and working together to get there. Always be ready to do something. Focus on what can be done now, big or small.

How we lead – and how we empower others – is rooted in our values.

Valley Leadership believes diversity, equity and inclusion create an environment that respects and values individual differences along varying dimensions. We value the person, any person, committed to leading Arizona forward.

Arizona’s can-do-attitude can solve anything. We continually look to our history to inspire and move us toward Arizona’s next big thing.

about.raw_text:
Big Brothers Big Sisters helps children realize their potential and build futures. We nurture children and strengthen communities. And we couldn’t do any of it without you.

At Big Brothers Big Sisters of Central Arizona, we are committed to building life-changing connections that ignite the power and promise of youth. Through our one-to-one mentoring programs and our school-based peer mentoring program, we create meaningful, relationships that empower young people to overcome challenges, build confidence, and pursue their dreams. Whether matched with an adult mentor or paired with a peer mentor at school, youth receive consistent guidance, encouragement, and a foundation of trust that helps them realize their full potential.

At BBBSAZ, mentorship is a powerful pathway to a brighter future. By standing with youth, we break barriers, open doors, and inspire lasting growth. Every mentoring relationship is intentionally built and supported to help young people thrive with confidence and resilience.

We envision a world where every child has the support and mentorship they need to thrive. Our goal is to ensure that all youth, regardless of their circumstances, have the resources and relationships necessary to reach their full potential.

We believe that when young people feel seen, heard, and empowered, they become confident leaders, changemakers, and contributors to a stronger community.

We value the acceptance of all, the celebration of unique differences, and the uncompromising inclusion of all perspectives. We work to ensure that all youth, regardless of background, have the support and resources they need to graduate high school, explore career pathways, and achieve success in life.

We value and recognize the remarkable resilience of youth and families and the ability of our community to work together to overcome obstacles and adapt to challenges.

We value transparency and uphold our commitment to the community and each other with integrity. Through taking ownership of our actions and their impact, we intentionally steward relationships and the resources entrusted to us to achieve our mission.

We value the ongoing evaluation and evolution of the agency to maximize our impact. We innovate with imagination and wisdom, transcending current notions of what is possible.

We value leading with empathy and blieve unconditional kindess has the power to form genuine connections and build community. We approach all interactions with authenticity and compassion to create mutual respect and understanding.

Big Sisters of Arizona was started by Justice Lorna Lockwood and 2 concerned Phoenix women.

Valley Big Brothers was started by Barry Starr, former Police Officer and City Councilman. He served as Executive Director for 17 years.

This is an exciting time for the Greater Phoenix Urban League (GPUL) as we continue celebrating our 80 th anniversary. And we have some exciting news. The Greater Phoenix Urban League is renovating our offices located at 1402 S. 7th Avenue! We are committed to keeping our valued stakeholders informed as we continue our mission of empowering the community throughout this renovation and relocation process.

Key Details of the Relocation

During this transition, all GPUL programs and operations will remain fully active and accessible. Our team is working diligently to ensure that services to the community, our partners, and supporters continue without interruption. If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact us at (602) 254-5611 or by completing the "contact us" form.

Thank you for your continued partnership and support of GPUL. Together, we will ensure that this temporary move leads to a stronger, more impactful future for our community.

George DeanPresident & CEOGreater Phoenix Urban League

The mission of Greater Phoenix Urban League is to be an agent of change; to support minorities and those in need in achieving economic and social equality through programs in economic empowerment, housing, education, civic engagement, and health and wellness.

Established in 1945, the Greater Phoenix Urban League, Inc. is a civil rights, social service, private 501c3 organization. The Greater Phoenix Urban League supports minority families and underserved populations by providing connections to employment, housing, health care, education, civic engagement, and advocacy.

Since our founding, we have served hundreds of thousands of individuals and continue to develop and expand our programs as we further the Urban League Movement in the greater Phoenix area, changing lives and empowering communities.

Today, vast disparities continue to exist in the United States, leaving generation after generation facing a cycle of poverty with deficient educational standards, unacceptably high unemployment, limited access to quality healthcare, and deplorable housing conditions.

At the Greater Phoenix Urban League, we assist disenfranchised and underserved groups to meet their basic needs, such as employment, education, and access to health care.

We serve individuals, families, and communities in need by offering a personalized, integrated approach to addiction treatment and behavioral health concerns. Junior Achievement of Arizona is an education solutions provider dedicated to accelerating opportunity and expanding pathways to economic mobility for young people across our state.Each year, we reach more than 150,000 learners through experiences that connect education to the real worldand help students build the skills, confidence, and networks needed for future success.

Supported by nearly 9,000 business and community volunteers annually,our programs foster financial literacy, career readiness, and entrepreneurial thinking through hands-on learning and meaningful industry connections.

Junior Achievement of Arizona is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization headquartered in Tempe, with an additional office in Tucson serving Southern Arizona. As a member of Junior Achievement USA, we collaborate with educators, businesses, and community partners statewide to help prepare Arizona’s future workforce.

Education should open doors to opportunity.But for many young people, there’s still a disconnect between what they learn in school and the skills, experiences, and networks needed to thrive in today’s economy.

We’re working to close that gap. By bringing together educators, volunteers, businesses, and communities, we help students connect learning to life, build confidence in their futures, and develop the skills needed for long-term success. When young people have access to opportunity, Arizona’s workforce, economy, and communities all benefit.

Junior Achievement is committed to promoting a brighter future for Arizona’s kids. Our innovative programs allow us to reach over 150,000 primarily low-income students annually. We serve students from all different geographic areas of Arizona, ranging from rural, suburban, urban, and tribal communities.

Junior Achievement was founded in 1919 by Theodore Vail, president of American Telephone & Telegraph; Horace Moses, president of Strathmore Paper Co.; and Senator Murray Crane of Massachusetts. They wanted to teach kids about business and how the United States economy functioned. The first JA program, The Company Program, was offered to high school students after school. Under the guidance of business mentors, students set up their own businesses and then manufactured and sold products and services.

In 1957, JA came west to Arizona, launching its first office in Tucson. In 1975, JA entered the classroom and gradually began offering programs at all grade levels, kindergarten through high school, expanding the curriculum to encompass financial literacy and career readiness education, in addition to the entrepreneurship training.

In 2001, JA launched the experiential program JA BizTown® at its current headquarters in Tempe, and then JA Finance Park® in 2009. In the following years, the organization added additional experiential and in-classroom programs that now reach 150,000 AZ students each year. Thanks to the support of local individuals, foundations and businesses, JA has served more than3 million students in its 65+ year history.

St. Mary’s Food Bank provides nutritious food to families, children, and seniors facing food insecurity. Each year, we distribute food to millions of neighbors throughout Arizona. Our efficient operations and purchasing power allow us to turn $1 donated into 5 meals.

We provide food, at No COST, to hundreds of partner agencies, who, in turn, give food to people in need. Our agency partners are food pantries, homeless shelters, meal centers, domestic violence shelters, afterschool programs for at-risk children, low-income senior living centers, etc. By donating to St. Mary’s, you are supporting hundreds of local nonprofit organizations and helping millions of people each year.

This all started right here at the World’s First Food Bank.

In 1967, John van Hengel was volunteering at a local soup kitchen, serving dinner to those in need when a young mother told him that she depended on soup kitchens and food from grocery store dumpsters to feed her children. Van Hengel’s heart was broken. His conversation with the young woman ignited a desire to help hungry families like hers, so he came up with the idea of a “Food Bank,” where individuals and companies with excess food could “deposit” it, and those in need could “withdraw” it.

His local parish, St. Mary’s Basilica in downtown Phoenix, gave him $3,000 and an abandoned building where he was able to turn his dream into reality. In gratitude, he named it “St. Mary’s Food Bank.” He then went on to become the founder of several other food banks across the country and even founded the national organization America’s Second Harvest (known today as Feeding America). Years later, van Hengel also founded the Global Food Banking Network. John van Hengel is rightly referred to as “the father of food banking” and it all started right here at St. Mary’s Food Bank in Phoenix, Arizona.

Today, St. Mary’s Food Bank is one of the largest food banks in the world, and is proud to be a Four Star charity with Charity Navigator and one of Americas Top 100 Charities by Forbes. St. Mary’s is also the Largest Phoenix-Area Nonprofit Organization for Service Assistance by Phoenix Business Journal.

Bridging the gap for Arizona communities with nourishment for today and hope for tomorrow.

brings more than 30 years of experience in the food and grocery industry with a notable background at Target and various food manufacturers. His dedication to community service is evident through his 20 years on non-profit boards, focusing on immigrant and refugee communities. In 2023, Milt and his wife moved from Minnesota to Arizona to lead St. Mary’s Food Bank. He has three college-aged sons, all born within 13 months of each other.

The Valley of the Sun YMCA is located on the ancestorial lands of indigenous first peoples; past, present, and future. We respectfully acknowledge Arizona’s twenty-two Native Nations that have inhabited this land for centuries. Our programs and branches occupy ancestral territories of Indigenous peoples, including the Akimel O’odham (Pima) and Piipaash (Maricopa) Indian Communities, in the Salt River Valley; the Hopi Indian Community in Northern Arizona; and the Yavapai-Apache Indian Community in Prescott Arizona, whose care and keeping of these lands allows us to be here today.

The YMCA is committed to building meaningful and lasting connections with Tribal Nations and Native communities. The Valley of the Sun YMCA welcomes members of all Native nations to our locations and programs.

The Valley of the Sun YMCA touches the lives of individuals and families through programs, activities, events, and mission outreach. More than 1,000,000 people walk through our doors each year seeking a community to call home, and opportunities to build a brighter tomorrow.

To advance research and provide a lifetime of support for individuals with autism and their families.

People with autism meaningfully integrated into inclusive communities.

Established in 1997, Southwest Autism Research & Resource Center (SARRC) is an internationally recognized nonprofit that conducts innovative research, provides evidence-based practices, disseminates effective training and builds inclusive communities for individuals with autism and their families. SARRC is dedicated to autism research, education, evidence-based treatment, and community outreach. Additionally, SARRC is one of the only autism organizations in the world that provides a lifetime of services for individuals and their families while also conducting cutting-edge research.

We’re also an entrepreneurial nonprofit, with less than three percent of annual revenue coming from state and federal funding. Our 18,000-square-foot Campus for Exceptional Children and our 10,000-square-foot Colonel Harland D. Sanders Center for Autism Studies, co-located with our Vocational & Life Skills Academy, are state-of-the-art clinical centers that serve as models for similar research and resource facilities.

Learn how SARRC will put effective services within reach of every Arizonan by 2030here.

SARRC’s clinical model is grounded in applied behavior analysis (ABA) with a particular focus on naturalistic behavioral interventions in inclusive environments, including but not limited to: home, school, job or community. SARRC provides support through children’s services, family services, teen and adult services, diagnostic services, community services, and ongoing research studies.

Each of SARRC’s programs, classes, and trainings are guided by best practice models; the most currently available science; increasing independence and producing meaningful outcomes; and the individualized needs of the children, teens, adults, and families we serve.

About Scouting Arizona, Grand Canyon Council

The Boy Scouts of America (BSA), was incorporated on February 8, 1910, and chartered by Congress in 1916. Its purpose is to provide young adults an effective educational program designed to build desirable qualities of character, to train in the responsibilities of participating citizenship and to develop in them personal fitness. Community groups such as religious, educational, civic, fraternal, business, labor, governmental bodies, corporations, professional associations, and groups of citizens who have compatible goals and utilize the program provided accomplish the purpose by the Boy Scouts of America on the local level.

The mission of Grand Canyon Council is to strengthen and expand Scouting in Arizona by building strong units, empowering leaders, and delivering programs and camps that enrich the local Scouting experience.

Together, volunteer and professional Scouters create an environment where every young person can discover their path, live the ideals of the Scout Oath, Law, and Motto, and grow into the best version of themselves.

Want more information on Scouting America or looking to connect with one of our staff members?

SERVICES OF THE LOCAL COUNCIL

The National Council, Scouting America, charters the Scouting Arizona, Grand Canyon Council to serve local chartered organizations and potential chartered organizations. The Council serves institutions through a large number of volunteers and a professional staff that supports the volunteer leadership by providing day-to-day administration. Community groups are supported by registration of members and leaders, advancement programs, communications, commissioner service, training of unit leadership, program enrichment activities, camping facilities, as well as volunteer recognition items, program supplies, planning materials, insurance and monthly round tables.

COUNCIL OPERATING PRINCIPLES

Scouting Arizona, Grand Canyon Council, Inc., is the legally and financially independent nonprofit organization chartered by BSA to deliver Scouting programs throughout most of central and northern Arizona, as well as the greater Yuma area.

The council is incorporated in Arizona and registered with the Arizona Corporation Commission. It is governed by its Articles of Incorporation and Bylaws. An all-volunteer Executive Board is elected each year at the Annual Business Meeting. Among its many responsibilities, the board is charged with hiring a Scout Executive to oversee and lead daily operations. A list of the current Executive Board is available at:Council Leadership

about.raw_text:
Through the power of serving over 125 agency partners, the dedication of our suppliers, and the generous support of our communities, we’re building a stronger, more united Arizona.

Our roots run deep in Arizona’s East Valley, where our mission to end hunger began in July 1983. Originally founded as United Food Distribution Center, Inc., United Food Bank was born from a collaborative effort between local cities and United Way organizations.

In our first year, we partnered with 28 community organizations to collect and distribute food to families in need. Many of those early partners are still with us today.

By 1985, we expanded our reach to serve Gila, Pinal, and parts of Apache and Navajo counties, alongside Maricopa County’s East Valley. As the needs of these communities grew, so did our organization.

Today, United Food Bank covers a vast service area of 19,608 square miles, including some of the most remote regions in Arizona. Our network of over 125 partner organizations helps us deliver critical support to families, children, and seniors across the state.

The food we provide comes from a powerful network of community support, with over 50% of the food arriving through our Grocery Rescue program. This program allows us to gather fresh, nutritious food from local grocery stores that would otherwise go to waste, including fruits, vegetables, dairy, meats, and shelf-stable items. Thanks to this initiative, we can provide quality food to our neighbors in need while also reducing food waste.

Our community’s generosity is woven into everything we do. Individual donors, local food drives, and caring partners all play vital roles in helping us stock our shelves. Partnerships with grocers and food producers also make a huge impact, allowing us to receive large, timely donations that keep our pantry well-supplied year-round. While we occasionally purchase food to ensure a balanced variety, every donation and dollar help provide meals to those in need.

We also receive support from federal programs, which provide additional staples to round out our offerings and help us meet the needs of our community. All of these contributions come together to create a vital safety net.

We work with community partners across our service area that operate food programs like food pantries, meal sites, after-school youth meal programs, as well as distributing food on our own through our mobile pantries.

Whether it’s food or funds, your contribution is appreciated. Food drives help replenish our shelves but monetary donations have an even greater impact. Through our partnerships,every $1 donated enables us to distribute three meals to people in need. Your financial support allows us to secure truckloads of nutritious food at minimal costs.

As Partners in Purpose, United Food Bank and Waste Not collaborate to ensure that surplus food is transformed into meals for those in need, driving impactful hunger relief efforts across Arizona.

We provide care that honors the diverse traditions, languages, and experiences of the people we serve. Our English and Spanish speaking staff speak your language and understand our community, creating an environment where you can feel seen, heard, and respected.

From the moment you walk through our doors, you'll experience person-centered care designed around your needs and your family's wellbeing. We believe in equitable access to services and offer comprehensive care regardless of your ability to pay, because your health should never depend on your income.

Call us at(602) 258-6797or use ourpatient portalto get connected to our care across Phoenix, Mesa, and surrounding areas.

**This health center receives HHS funding and has Federal Public Health Service (PHS) deemed status with respect to certain health or health-related claims, including medical malpractice claims, for itself and its covered individuals.

Our work is rooted in compassion, equity, and community empowerment:

These principles guide every interaction, every service, and every decision we make. They reflect our commitment to preserving the dignity of all people while creating the standards by which others are measured.

Valle Del Sol Community Health was founded in 1970 by social justice activists who saw a critical gap in behavioral health and social support services for Latino and underserved communities in Phoenix. What began as a civil rights organization has grown into a trusted leader in integrated healthcare, rooted in the belief that everyone deserves compassionate, culturally aligned care. For over five decades, we've listened to our community and evolved our services to meet their needs, from adding youth services in the mid-70s to incorporating primary care in 2011.

Today, we operate multiple clinics throughout the Phoenix metropolitan area and continue to innovate. OurHispanic Leadership Instituteempowers the next generation of diverse leaders, and our annualProfiles of Success Hispanic Leadership Awards Dinnercelebrates Latino leadership across Arizona—making us more than a health center, but a true community anchor.

Valle Del Sol Community Health is guided by an executive team deeply committed to our mission and immersed in the communities we serve. Our leaders bring decades of experience in healthcare, community advocacy, and organizational excellence, ensuring Valle Del Sol Community Health remains responsive to community needs while maintaining the highest standards of care.

They lead with authentic empathy, honoring our civil rights legacy while driving innovation across our growing network of clinics throughout the Phoenix metropolitan area.Meet the Team Behind Valle Del Sol Community Health

Volunteers and supporters make it possible for us to bring transformative arts programs to children who have experienced abuse, neglect, or homelessness. Whether you host an art supply drive, become a volunteer mentor, or make a donation — your contribution is crucial.

With the Arizona Foster Care tax credit, you can direct your tax dollars to help bring transformative arts programs to children affected by trauma.

Art Heals Arizona (formerly Art Heals Arizona) accepts a variety of in-kind goods and services to enhance the experience for our children and volunteers. This is an ongoing need as our programs happen year round.

Each year, over 78,600 Arizona children experience the trauma of abuse, neglect, and homelessness.

Research shows that in order to process toxic stress caused by trauma, children need positive experiences and supportive relationships.

We use the arts to provide opportunities for children to express themselves and connect with volunteer mentors.

Since our founding in 1970, Breakthrough T1D has played a critical role in every major type 1 diabetes milestone.

Founded in 1970 by families whose loved ones had been diagnosed with type 1 diabetes (T1D), Breakthrough T1D is a tax-exempt nonprofit 501(c)3 organization.

We are opening doors that were once closed by T1D diagnosis. We lead the way to more effective solutions by connecting the brightest minds to advance treatments, influence policy, and improve access to care.​ By driving innovation forward, Breakthrough T1D will make type 1 diabetes a condition of the past.

Accelerating life-changing breakthroughs to cure, prevent, and treat type 1 diabetes and its complications.

As we drive toward curing type 1 diabetes, we help make everyday life better for the people who face it.

Breakthrough T1D invests in the most promising research to turn ideas into life-changing therapies, including cures.

Learn how we’re accelerating breakthroughs to improve lives while driving toward cures.

Our mission requires strong partnerships with government leaders, regulatory officials, and healthcare coverage providers.

No organization does more to improve lives and drive toward cures for type 1 diabetes.

Breakthrough T1D was founded by volunteers, and today is led by a powerful partnership between our most dedicated volunteer leaders and our executive team—most of whom either live with type 1 diabetes or have loved ones with the condition. Aaron J. Kowalski, Ph.D., is the first person with T1D to serve as our organization’s Chief Executive Officer.

Achieving our vision of a world without T1D requires global collaboration. Approximately 9 million people around the world live with the condition. Our five affiliates—Australia, Canada, Israel, the Netherlands, and the United Kingdom—are pivotal partners in breaking barriers to therapy access and in funding research for life-changing T1D breakthroughs.

Breakthrough T1D doesn’t have laboratories. Our field of play is the global ecosystem of academia, industry, and governments with the means and the expertise to one day cure T1D.
about.description: At Breakthrough T1D, we advance type 1 diabetes treatments, influence policy, and make everyday life better for everyone living with T1D.

Our vision is a better world shaped by Frank Lloyd Wright’s legacy and ideas, inspiring how we live, learn, and build.

We connect people to the continued relevance of Frank Lloyd Wright’s architectural legacy; we preserve the buildings, landscapes, and collections of Taliesin and Taliesin West; and we advance the impact of architecture and design.

We embrace Wright’s philosophy and transform it into actions for a thriving future.

Photo: © 2017, Andrew Pielage

Preserving the buildings, landscapes, collections, and communities of Taliesin and Taliesin West, Frank Lloyd Wright’s own homes and studios and the most personal expressions of his work, to provide experiences that will inspire and challenge visitors to build and live better.

Photo: © 2017, Andrew Pielage

Influencing the growth of architecture, design, and planning by collaborating with universities, scholars, practitioners, and industry at the intersection of nature and the built environment.

Photo: © 2017, Andrew Pielage

Educating a worldwide audience about the continued relevance of Wright’s architectural and cultural legacy through tours, exhibits, performances, school and youth programs, and digital engagement.

The Frank Lloyd Wright Foundation’s policy on inclusion, diversity, equity, and accessibility seeks to extend Frank Lloyd Wright’s core belief system in all of our work.

Frank Lloyd Wright licensed products are desired by people who appreciategreat designandrefined style.

In 1955, Frank Lloyd Wright began to license his work to make his designs more broadly available, rather than restricted to clients of his practice. For this project, Wright created original designs for the Taliesin Ensemble of products in partnership with leading design brands. Beginning with that original work and continuing today, Frank Lloyd Wright licensed products represent refined style, through the expression of the integral relationships between the natural and the man-made, and between material and design. The program encompasses more than one thousand primary design references, accompanied by the most iconic name in architecture and design.

For more than 45 years we have been providing convenient, affordable primary healthcare services for patients from all walks of life, through all stages in life. Each year we serve nearly 115,000 patients ranging from Goodyear to Tempe, Glendale to South Phoenix and more.

Mountain Park Health Center is a nonprofit community health center. We believe in challenging the ordinary, making time for human connection, and pursuing excellence. We work with the communities we serve to sustain and improve health by providing affordable primary  healthcare.

Mountain Park believes in being proactive about your health. We know that healthcare education, screenings and access to affordable medications help prevent serious health problems. Proactive healthcare can also help manage chronic conditions, like obesity and diabetes, and detect diseases in the most treatable stages. We are here for you anytime you need.

Our caring staff is here to help you navigateAHCCCSor the health insurance marketplace. We can also help you apply forSNAP(formerly called food stamps) andTANF(cash assistance). If you don’t have health insurance, we will work with you to make healthcare affordable through ourSliding Fee Discount Programand other resources.Click hereto learn more or to make an appointment with our eligibility team.

We always put our patients first. As a Patient Centered Medical Home, Mountain Park offers all the care you need in one single place. You’ll have access to an entire Care Team of primary care physicians, physician’s assistants, nurse practitioners, clinical pharmacists, behavioral health consultants and registered dietitians all in one exam room.

Mountain Park Health Center has been there for our community since 1980. We work with other organizations to provide our patients high-quality, affordable care. Over the years, our dedication to our patients and their families has paid off and Mountain Park has been presented various awards. Here are some of the organizations that have recognized our work:

All Mountain Park clinics are accredited by The Joint Commission, which accredits healthcare organizations across the nation. This accreditation reflects Mountain Park’s commitment to quality, safety and employee education.To maintain the commission’s Gold Seal of Approval™, Mountain Park demonstrates its commitment to certain performance standards and must undergo an on-site survey by a Joint Commission survey team at least every three years.Learn More

Mountain Park Health Center is a deemed facility under the Health Resources and Services Administration’s Federal Tort Claims Act (FTCA).

This health center is a Health Center Program grantee under 42 U.S.C. 254b, and a deemed Public Health Service employee under 42 U.S.C. 233(g)-(n).

For nearly five decades, Child Crisis Arizona has supported vulnerable children, youth, and families in our community, offering help during crises and working to strengthen families and prevent future challenges.

Our mission is to provide a safe environment for children and youth, free from abuse and neglect, by fostering strong, successful families through prevention, intervention, and education programs focused on creating safe kids and strong families.

The kindness and generosity of our supporters makes brighter futures possible for children and families in our community. Together, we are creating safety, stability, and opportunities for those who need it most.

We prioritize financial transparency as a key aspect of our integrity and accountability. We provide easy access to our financial statements and performance quality improvement scorecard, ensuring our community can see how contributions directly support vulnerable children and families.

Child Crisis Arizona raises awareness about critical issues affecting children and families in our community through impactful initiatives and success stories.

Supporters like you give at risk kids the chance to live safe, happy lives. There are creative ways to make a major impact.

Learn more about what we do and stay up to date on our latest news and events. Discover valuable resources, impactful initiatives, and inspiring success stories that highlight our commitment to supporting Arizona’s children and families.
